load_data – Load

src/load_data.py

Load cleaned GradCafe applicant data into PostgreSQL.

This module is the database-loading stage of the ETL pipeline. It reads the LLM-extended JSON produced by the cleaning step, converts free-form string fields ("Added on Feb 17, 2026", "GPA 3.85", "GRE V 160") into typed Python values, and bulk-upserts them into the applicants table.

Connection settings come from the standard libpq environment variables (PGDATABASE, PGUSER, PGPASSWORD, PGHOST, PGPORT) and can be overridden on the command line.

Example:

python load_data.py --json-file llm_extend_applicant_data.json --create-db
load_data.parse_date_added(value)[source]

Parse an "Added on <Mon DD, YYYY>" string into a datetime.date.

Parameters:

value (str or None) – Raw date_added string, e.g. "Added on Feb 17, 2026".

Returns:

The parsed date, or None if the value is empty, does not match the expected prefix, or has an unparseable date.

Return type:

datetime.date or None

>>> parse_date_added("Added on Feb 17, 2026")
datetime.date(2026, 2, 17)
load_data.parse_gpa(value)[source]

Parse a "GPA <value>" string, e.g. "GPA 3.85", into a float.

Some entries use a weighted/non-4.0 scale (values up to ~4.9 appear in the data), so this does not clamp or reject those – it returns whatever number was reported, keeping the column an honest float rather than silently dropping legitimate values or tripping a CHECK constraint that would abort the whole batch insert.

Parameters:

value (str or None) – Raw GPA string.

Returns:

The numeric GPA, or None if missing or unparseable.

Return type:

float or None

load_data.parse_score(value)[source]

Extract a trailing numeric GRE score from a free-form string.

Works for Quant, Verbal and Analytical Writing, e.g. "GRE 166", "GRE V 160" or "GRE AW 4.5". Returns None (rather than raising) for missing or unparseable values so a record with no GRE scores never blocks the load.

Parameters:

value (str or None) – Raw score string.

Returns:

The score as a float, or None.

Return type:

float or None

load_data.clean_text(value)[source]

Strip surrounding whitespace and normalise empty strings to None.

Parameters:

value (str or None) – Text to clean.

Returns:

The stripped string, or None if it was None or blank.

Return type:

str or None

load_data.load_records(path)[source]

Read the source JSON file into a list of applicant dictionaries.

Parameters:

path (pathlib.Path) – Path to a JSON file containing a list of applicant objects.

Returns:

The decoded list of records.

Return type:

list[dict[str, Any]]

Raises:

  • FileNotFoundError – If path does not exist.

  • json.JSONDecodeError – If the file is not valid JSON.

load_data.to_row(rec)[source]

Convert one JSON record into a parameter tuple for INSERT_SQL.

The tuple order matches the column list in INSERT_SQL: program, comments, date_added, url, status, term, us_or_international, gpa, gre, gre_v, gre_aw, degree, llm_generated_program, llm_generated_university.

Parameters:

rec (dict[str, Any]) – A single applicant record from the JSON file.

Returns:

A 14-element tuple of typed column values.

Return type:

tuple

load_data.create_database_if_missing(dbname, user, password, host, port)[source]

Create the target database if it does not already exist.

Connects to the postgres maintenance database with autocommit enabled (CREATE DATABASE cannot run inside a transaction). The connecting role needs the CREATEDB privilege.

Parameters:

  • dbname (str) – Name of the database to create.

  • user (str | None) – PostgreSQL role name.

  • password (str | None) – Password for user (None to rely on PGPASSWORD or ~/.pgpass).

  • host (str) – Database host.

  • port (str) – Database port.

Return type:

None

load_data.CREATE_TABLE_SQL = '\nCREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS applicants (\n    p_id                        SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,   -- unique identifier\n    program                     TEXT NOT NULL,        -- University and Department/Program\n    comments                    TEXT,                 -- applicant comments\n    date_added                  DATE,                 -- date entry was added\n    url                         TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE, -- link to Grad Cafe entry (natural key)\n    status                      TEXT,                 -- admission status\n    term                        TEXT,                 -- intended start term\n    us_or_international         TEXT,                 -- applicant nationality classification\n    gpa                         REAL,                 -- applicant GPA\n    gre                         REAL,                 -- GRE Quantitative score\n    gre_v                       REAL,                 -- GRE Verbal score\n    gre_aw                      REAL,                 -- GRE Analytical Writing score\n    degree                      TEXT,                 -- degree type\n    llm_generated_program       TEXT,                 -- LLM-generated department/program\n    llm_generated_university    TEXT                  -- LLM-generated university\n);\n\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_applicants_university  ON applicants (llm_generated_university);\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_applicants_program      ON applicants (llm_generated_program);\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_applicants_term         ON applicants (term);\nCREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_applicants_degree       ON applicants (degree);\n'

DDL for the applicants table and its lookup indexes. Idempotent (IF NOT EXISTS) so it is safe to run on every load.

load_data.MIGRATE_SQL = '\nALTER TABLE applicants DROP CONSTRAINT IF EXISTS applicants_gpa_check;\n'

Brings a table created by an older version of this script up to date (drops a legacy GPA CHECK constraint that rejected weighted GPAs).

load_data.INSERT_SQL = '\nINSERT INTO applicants (\n    program, comments, date_added, url, status, term,\n    us_or_international, gpa, gre, gre_v, gre_aw, degree,\n    llm_generated_program, llm_generated_university\n) VALUES (\n    %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s, %s\n)\nON CONFLICT (url) DO UPDATE SET\n    program                  = EXCLUDED.program,\n    comments                 = EXCLUDED.comments,\n    date_added               = EXCLUDED.date_added,\n    status                   = EXCLUDED.status,\n    term                     = EXCLUDED.term,\n    us_or_international      = EXCLUDED.us_or_international,\n    gpa                      = EXCLUDED.gpa,\n    gre                      = EXCLUDED.gre,\n    gre_v                    = EXCLUDED.gre_v,\n    gre_aw                   = EXCLUDED.gre_aw,\n    degree                   = EXCLUDED.degree,\n    llm_generated_program    = EXCLUDED.llm_generated_program,\n    llm_generated_university = EXCLUDED.llm_generated_university;\n'

Parameterised upsert keyed on url. Re-running the loader refreshes every column of existing rows instead of failing on the UNIQUE constraint.

load_data.main()[source]

Command-line entry point: parse arguments and load the JSON file.

Steps:

  1. Optionally create the database (--create-db).

  2. Read the JSON file and convert every record with to_row().

  3. Run CREATE_TABLE_SQL and MIGRATE_SQL.

  4. Bulk-upsert all rows with INSERT_SQL in a single transaction, rolling back on any error.

Raises:

Exception – Re-raises any database error after rolling back.

Return type:

None
